$schema_note: Single-cell mechanics as a boolean report card. Each axis maps to a `behavior`-marked test in tests/test_model_behavior.py (pytest-as-evidence). The measurement is procedural + single-cell (run via pytest); only the pass/fail/skip RESULT flows through the shared grader/renderer. A skipped test (missing checkpoint/trajectory) renders `ungraded`, not a failure.
title: Single-cell mechanics

stimulus.summary: single cell from a pre-division checkpoint (no ensemble) · 7 invariant checks via pytest -m behavior
stimulus.source: single cell from a pre-division checkpoint (tests/fixtures/pre_division_state.json.gz) + single-cell trajectory

single_cell_mechanics.mass_doubles.label: Dry mass roughly doubles
single_cell_mechanics.mass_doubles.how: Over a complete cycle the cell accumulates ~1.5-2.5x initial dry mass (rejects both stalls and runaway growth).

single_cell_mechanics.monotone_growth.label: Growth is monotone (no stalls)
single_cell_mechanics.monotone_growth.how: No >60s interval where dry mass is non-increasing; a stall means a listener crashed or metabolism shut off.

single_cell_mechanics.replication_window.label: Replication completes in window
single_cell_mechanics.replication_window.how: First appearance of 2 full chromosomes lands in a biologically reasonable window (~[900, 1800] s).

single_cell_mechanics.forks_persist.label: Forks persist mid-cycle
single_cell_mechanics.forks_persist.how: At least 3 mid-cycle snapshots have active replication forks (protects against forks terminating immediately).

single_cell_mechanics.conserves_bulk.label: Division conserves bulk
single_cell_mechanics.conserves_bulk.how: Invoking the divide machinery yields two daughters with populated bulk arrays; mother count == d1 + d2.

single_cell_mechanics.conserves_chromoso.label: Division conserves chromosomes
single_cell_mechanics.conserves_chromoso.how: Full chromosomes split across division without creation/destruction (mother == d1 + d2).

single_cell_mechanics.daughters_grow.label: Daughters build and grow
single_cell_mechanics.daughters_grow.how: Both daughters build from the split state and each gains >=0.5 fg dry mass over a short run — the strongest evidence the full machinery is wired through division.

findings: Single-cell mechanical invariants, graded as pytest-as-evidence: the result of the `behavior`-marked single-cell checks flows through the shared boolean criterion. A skipped check (missing checkpoint/trajectory) is `ungraded`, not a pass or fail.
These are preconditions the population (ensemble) cards assume; they compose with those cards (e.g. as a fast pre-merge gate) but are graded as a distinct, single-cell kind of behavioral check.
